Commentary.Commentary: We are set to begin Sri Lanka's second innings. The England players are out in the middle. Lahiru Thirimanne and Kusal Perera will open the innings for Sri Lanka. Stuart Broad will start the proceedings for England.

Sri Lanka would look to bat better in their second innings. On the other hand, England would look to pick up quick wickets and put pressure on Sri Lanka. Join us in a while for the second session.

Sri Lankan bowlers had to work hard throughout the innings. Dilruwan Perera managed to take 4 wickets while Lasith Embuldeniya toiled hard for his 3 wickets. But it was Asitha Fernando who broke the Root-Buttler stand after a ball change, and got the wickets of Buttler and Curran in consecutive balls this morning. But Sri Lanka might think that they would have done better to restrict England to a smaller score in their home conditions.

For England, the duo of Root and Buttler scored at a brisk rate in the first half an hour. Root got to his 4th double ton in the process and batted superbly hardly giving any chance to the bowlers. Buttler and Curran though were dismissed by Fernando in successive balls, leaving the tail to bat with the skipper. The tail-enders hardly showed any resistance and kept losing their wickets at regular intervals. Root was eventually dismissed but only after scoring 228. England's batting did well overall with Bairstow scoring a fine 47, and the debutant Dan Lawrence shining brightly with a score of 73. But it was all Joe Root, who made sure that England breach the 400-run mark.

So this session saw Sri Lankan bowlers more into action. Although England are way ahead in the game with a massive lead of 286 runs, Sri Lanka have done well to take the remaining 6 wickets. The umpires have decided to take Lunch as well.

We are all set to begin Day 3. The Sri Lanka players are out in the middle. Joe Root and Jos Buttler will resume their innings for England. Asitha Fernando will start the proceedings for Day 3.

Dan Lawrence is down for an interview. He says that yesterday was a very special day for him. He adds that he stayed true to his game plan, and was looking to get runs quickly against the spinners. Also adds that it was good fun batting with the skipper. On his chat with Kallis, he says they had a chat about the mindset required playing in these conditions, and about playing the first 20 minutes. Says that it was great fun with Root, praises him for playing spin nicely and was looking to learn from his skipper. He says they are looking to bat long and build a massive lead.

Pitch Report - Russel Arnold says that the ball was turning and bouncing yesterday. He adds that there is rough areas all over the pitch and there are footmarks too, which can help the bowlers. Also adds that Sri Lanka will need to bat very well to survive as there will be lot of turn on the pitch as England will put them under scoreboard pressure.

Hello and welcome to Day 3 of the first Test between England and Sri Lanka. Day 3 is usually the moving day of a Test match, but this match has been moving away from the hosts right from Day 1. After getting out for a paltry 135, Day 2 saw England pile on the misery over the island nation with a lead of 185 runs. England skipper Root is unbeaten on 168 and would be eager to score a double ton today. Day 2 saw rain play a spoilsport with the entire last session getting washed out. Hope the rain stays away today and we get a full day's play starting with the morning session coming up very shortly.
... Day 3, Session 1 ...

So, That's it from Day 2. It was a day where Rain and Root had their say. Rest all were just spectators. Play on Day 3 will start 15 minutes early to compensate for the lost time and overs. The weather though does not look that great, as we might have a wet day, on the moving day of this Test match. To know more about where this Test heads join us at 0945 local (0400 GMT). Till then take care, cheers and goodbye.

Sri Lankan bowlers were better than day 1 but they hardly took any wickets to show the same. With Embuldeniya getting rid of Bairstow earlier in the morning, the Lankans would have thought of making a comeback. But their confidence was shattered as their spinners couldn't apply the pressure on the duo of Root and Lawrence and went for easy runs. To add to it shoddy catching rubbed salt on their wound. Dilruwan Perera did manage to get the wicket of Lawrence, but it was a complete no show from the entire bowling group.

After a delay of around an hour, England began Day 2 trailing by 8 runs and with two set batsmen Joe Root and Jonny Bairstow at the crease. The latter was out on the 8th ball of the morning, 3 runs short of his half-century. The debutant Dan Lawrence came to the crease and acted a perfect second fiddle to his skipper. Both of them amassed a mammoth 173-run partnership for the 4th wicket. In the process, Root completed his 18th test ton while the debutant scored a well compiled 73. His innings though was cut short by Dilruwan Perera. He though impressed one and all with his temperament against the spinners. Root is still unbeaten on 168 and has Buttler for his company at the crease. The duo will look to up the ante tomorrow.

So, THAT WILL BE STUMPS ON DAY 2! The day started off with rain and fittingly ends with rain playing spoilsport. Amidst the rain break, sandwiched was a Joe Root masterclass who got to his 18th Test ton and thereby took England to a considerable lead of 185 runs.

The lead for England is nearing the 200-run mark. Sri Lanka would want to see the back of Joe Root as quickly as possible in the final session as Root and Buttler can take the game away from them in no time. Buttler is still new to the crease as the Lankans would not want this partnership to grow. An interesting final session of the other side of this break in about 20 minutes. Stay tuned.

Sri Lankan bowlers toiled hard but were unable to get past the duo of Root and Lawrence. A half chance of Lawrence was spilled down by Kusal Mendis at second slip. They took the new ball and finally Dilruwan Perera was rewarded with the wicket of Lawrence. The pitch has been slow but the Sri Lankan spinners have not been able to put pressure on the English batsmen.

Just after Lunch, Root completed his 18th Test ton and his partner Dan Lawrence played beautifully to bring up his maiden half century. Both of them were involved in a massive 173-run partnership. The debutant looked good for his century but was out caught at short leg off Dilruwan Perera. Buttler joined his skipper in the middle and has kept the scoreboard ticking. Root, meanwhile has been unbeaten on 168, and would like to get a double here.

It has been England's session completely. Joe Root and the debutant Lawrence got to their respective milestones and have put England in a commanding position. 114 runs have been scored and just 1 wicket has been lost by England.

Sri Lanka's bowling was way better then what they displayed in the last session of Day 1. The gave a bit more flight and tried to extract the turn and bounce available around the off stump line off the right handed batsmen. They just managed to pick up a lone wicket of Jonny Bairstow as a couple of edges went past the slips and the close in fielders. They would though be disappointed not to get Root's wicket as they know that he is the one who can take the game away from them at any instance.

After a rain curtailed start, Sri Lanka started brilliantly as the bowled in right areas to extract the turn and bounce on offer. Embuldeniya was lucky of the three spinners as he scalped Jonny Bairstow, who fell short by just three runs of a well deserved half ton. Since then the debutant Dan Lawrence has played some good cricket as he has managed to get to 40 runs in no time as England went onto take the lead to 71 runs. Root too played his strokes as he went to Lunch unbeaten on 99 runs.
A brilliant session for the hosts. Despite losing Bairstow early,  they have managed to score at a brisk pace. The young lad Lawrence is playing a perfect foil to his skipper.

Sri Lanka Head Coach Mickey Arthur is down for a chat. He says that yesterday was very disappointing in all aspects. He says they gave away their first 6 wickets and it was not England who took those. Also disappointed with the way their senior players got out. He says they played way better in South Africa than they did yesterday. He says that they had a tough chat last night and looks forward for the team to bounce back. He says they were searching for wickets in the last session yesterday, but today they need to be patient and stop searching for wickets today. He is optimistic about his team's chances.

Pitch Report - Rusell Arnold is down as the pitch doctor and he managed to get a sneak-peek at the pitch just before the covers came on and he says the pitch had turn and bounce and there is turn from a good length spot outside off for the right-handed batsman. He further mentions that if the ball turns the outside edge comes into play and if he doesn't then the inside edge gets threatened. Further praises Jonny Bairstow and Joe Root for adjusting brilliantly to the spinners. He ends by saying that the pitch will do more today.

So fingers crossed at the moment.

Coming in to bat after an impressive bowling performance, England too started falsely as they lost their openers early, but the duo of the Jonny Bairstow and Joe Root have steadied the ship for England with an unbeaten stand of 110. England are trailing by just 8 runs with 8 wickets in hand, they would like to wipe out the deficit and look for a big lead. Can the Lankans restrict them to low score? or will England bat the hosts out of the game? Answers to all these questions coming up as the morning session on Day 2 unfolds very shortly.

The hosts after winning the toss, batted first but were bundled out for a paltry 135 runs in around 46 overs. None of their batsmen went on to make a big score. The absence of their skipper Dimuth Karunaratne hurt them the most at the top of the batting order. Kusal Perera, Angelo Mathews and skipper Dinesh Chandimal, all got starts but none capitalized on that to get to a substantial score. Dom Bess was the wrecker-in-chief with 5 wickets for England but before he came to the picture it was the double strike of Stuart Broad in the start that set the momentum in England's favour.

Day 1 of a Test match is very crucial for any team as that decides the momentum of the Test. Sri Lanka faltered there as they welcomed international cricket back after the COVID-19 pandemic. Being the home team they let go the advantage to the opposition by batting poorly thus playing the catching game in this Test.
... DAY 2, SESSION 1 ...

Right then, the Sri Lankans are going to have a tough session, back in the dressing room we meant, where Arthur is likely to slam them for their performance on Day 1. Can they look back and come stronger and restrict England from building a sizeable lead? Or will the English batters go about on their merry way? Join us at 1000 Local (0430 GMT) on Friday, 15th January 2021, for all the action from Day 2. Until then, cheers and take care....

Stuart Broad has been caught up for a quick chat. He says they were looking to build pressure by making the batsmen play and his plan was to change his pace, as the pitch was two-paced with some extra bounce. Also says it was a decent day for him, taking 3 wickets as a pacer in Sri Lanka. Says further that it was not a deliberate ball to Thirimanne, where he was caught at leg slip. But they had a plan to keep the fielder there. On bowling leg cutters, Stuart says he has worked on it and with experience has become braver to bowl that ball to a new batter. Says it was a classy performance from Jonny and Root to play nicely throughout the session. Also says Day 2 will be an important day for England, in context of the match.

Stepping out to bat in response, in their first innings, the English found themselves in a quagmire as they lost both their openers early. Just as it looked like Sri Lanka would make up for their poor effort with the bat, Root and Bairstow set right the English ship and steered them to safer shores, at close of play, with an unbeaten 110-run partnership. For Sri Lanka, Embuldeniya snared both the wickets while the rest have nothing to show, in their wickets column.

Earlier, after winning the toss, the home side opted to bat first. But it turned out to be a disaster for them as they lost their top-order pretty quickly. However, Angelo and Dinesh did well to bring the Lankans back on track. But once they fell, in successive overs, the writing was clear on the wall for Sri Lanka. They got bundled out for 135. Dom Bess got 5, Stuart Broad got 3, while Jack Leach picked up 1 wicket.

Well, easily the English's day it is. There was some minor scare for the visitors when they lost their openers early but Joe and Jonny have done well to stabilize the innings. The two Yorkshire batters have done really well here. It is due to their efforts that England now trail by just 8 runs, with 8 wickets still in hand.
